Consider a directed weighted graph G(V, E), where V is the set of vertices and E is the set of edges. Suppose we use adjacency list to implement the graph. Consider a sequence of |V| operations with each corresponding to a different vertex in V. For the operation for vertex v, the cost is assumed to be the number of outgoing edges from v.  (a) What is the cost of the worst possible single operation in this sequence of operations? (b) What is the average amortized cost of the above sequence of operations based on aggregate analysis?

message.content:
The worst possible single operation occurs when a vertex has the maximum number of outgoing edges, which in a simple directed graph is |V| - 1, since a vertex can have at most one outgoing edge to each of the other |V| - 1 vertices. For the aggregate analysis, we note that the total cost across all |V| operations equals the sum of the out-degrees of every vertex, which is simply |E|, because every edge in the graph contributes exactly once to the out-degree of its source vertex.

* Part (a): The cost of the worst possible single operation is **|V| - 1**, corresponding to a vertex that has an outgoing edge to every other vertex in the graph.
* Part (b): The average amortized cost per operation is **|E| / |V|**, derived by dividing the total aggregate cost |E| by the number of operations |V|.
